issue_context.title: kubectl get -o jsonpath no longer continues parsing an item when a key is encountered that has no value
issue_context.body:
#### What happened:

`kubectl get -o jsonpath` no longer continues parsing an item when a key is encountered that has no value.  This appears to be a behavior change introduced in Kubernetes version 1.22.

#### What you expected to happen:

`kubectl get -o jsonpath` will continue .

#### How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible):

Run the following commands against a cluster running CoreDNS pods in the `kube-system` namespace:

```
raw_run_as_user_results=$(kubectl get pods -n kube-system -l k8s-app=kube-dns -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{"SED_NEW_LINE_FILTER"}{"podName="}{.metadata.name}{":podNamespace="}{.metadata.namespace}{":podRunAsUser="}{.spec.securityContext.runAsUser}{":podRunAsNonRoot="}{.spec.securityContext.runAsNonRoot}{":"}{range .spec.containers[*]}{"containerName="}{.name}{":containerRunAsUser="}{.securityContext.runAsUser}{":containerRunAsNonRoot="}{.securityContext.runAsNonRoot}{":containerPrivileged="}{.securityContext.privileged}{":"}{end}{end}')
formatted_run_as_user_results=$(sed 's/SED_NEW_LINE_FILTER/\n/g' <<< "${raw_run_as_user_results}")
echo "${formatted_run_as_user_results}"
```

#### Anything else we need to know?:

Nothing.

#### Environment:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): v1.22.0
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration: N/A
- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`): N/A
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`): N/A
- Install tools: N/A
- Network plugin and version (if this is a network-related bug): N/A
- Others: N/A

review_comments: how is this related? I don't see it in the reverted PR.
this is a behaviour that got broken by the reverted commit. Ie the template got discarded after the `{.hello}` element.
shouldn't we have both cases tested, ie with and without end?

Should we test invalid syntaxes here? What should be the behaviour?
- the output is broken and outputs additional line (current behaviour)
- or should we fast fail with invalid syntax error? (would require changes)
it was kind of graceful before to leave out the `{end}`, just a little wrong. Could be get it working easily too?
In any case, I would rather try to avoid breaking behaviour that ran without error before. Fixing it is ok, but not suddenly fail.

I am not sure how easy that would be. 
But do we want to support an invalid syntax? I think it is a bit problematic of supporting this especially when you consider nested ranges. I would prefer an error here , but that would also break some scripts (more than keeping it failing slightly).

I think that the support for missing `{end}` was rather accidental than intentional. I'd prefer we stick with having code simple and complying to jsonpath standard, than over-complicated to support something not entirely correct.
I would prefer keeping graceful behaviour and not fix it and break users. But I am not blocking this. Both paths are acceptable.
